purpose: Passive pre-incident company exposure research; source selection and access validation.

summary.invite_sweep_status: Additional invite checks stopped when Telegram requested a wait; remaining invite candidates untested. Retry interval was not retained by the temporary research helper.

methodology: Vendor investigations and academic studies supplied source categories and discovery methods. Community directories were leads, not proof of identity or freshness.

108 public handles were tested sequentially with dark-mcp over stdio, sampling three recent visible posts per source. Five selected public feeds and one invite destination were inspected to a depth of 15.

Public channel metadata, active aliases and invite validity were inspected through the Telegram client API. Four invite-linked sources had history checked through dark-mcp; two were stale. Guest previews expire.

Search controls used OpenAI in five channels. Positive controls returned matches in Data Leak Monitor and vx-underground; the other three returned zero. This validates limited retrieval, not completeness.
No channels were joined, access requests submitted, Stars spent, purchases made, messages sent, attachments downloaded, or exposed credentials tested.
A current post may be a promotion, redirect, service event, or recycled old incident. Every recommended source needs ongoing content and identity review.

public_channels.assessment: Company/domain-oriented summaries are searchable; latest October post discusses older incidents. Posting date is not incident date. Verify each claim against its original source.

limitations: Public text only; archive/image-only leaks are not searchable with the current MCP.
User accounts and supergroups are unsupported by the current broadcast-only connector.
Invite preview preflight was a research helper outside the MCP; the MCP cannot renew preview access autonomously.
Global post search requires Premium on this account; channel-specific read/search and channel discovery worked.
No representative platform-wide sampling, coverage percentage, authenticity verification, or claim of absence is supported.
Breachsense and deepdarkCTI have substantial list overlap and are treated as one discovery pool, not independent identity corroboration.

research_references.use: TeleHunt: contextual snowball discovery using handles, invite links and forwards; research dataset is not a current operational source list.
DarkGram: demonstrates cybercrime-channel diversity and migrations; its historical sample is not present-day coverage.
Credential exposure source categories; named brands do not establish current handles.
Historical channel descriptions and researcher-vs-actor distinctions.
Channel-role taxonomy and migration leads; activity labels independently rechecked.
Chthonic, Eternity and Xtreme are vendor-reported leads; no current matching channel identity/access established in this run.
Temporary read access without joining and its expiry.
Independent campaign context for AI-provider-key exposure; does not authenticate the particular Telegram seller.
